title: USPSTF Statin Use for Primary Prevention of CVD (summary)
text: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) recommends that clinicians prescribe a statin for the primary prevention of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in adults aged 40 to 75 years who have one or more CVD risk factors (such as dyslipidemia, diabetes, hypertension, or smoking) and an estimated 10-year CVD event risk of 10% or greater. For adults aged 40 to 75 years with CVD risk factors and a 10-year CVD risk of 7.5% to less than 10%, the decision to initiate a statin should be individualized. The USPSTF concludes that evidence is insufficient for adults 76 years or older. Shared decision-making is important.

title: ACC/AHA Blood Pressure Guideline Categories (summary)
text: According to ACC/AHA blood pressure categories commonly used in U.S. practice: Normal blood pressure is less than 120/80 mm Hg. Elevated blood pressure is systolic 120-129 and diastolic less than 80. Stage 1 hypertension is systolic 130-139 or diastolic 80-89. Stage 2 hypertension is systolic at least 140 or diastolic at least 90. Lifestyle measures include sodium reduction, physical activity, weight management, and limiting alcohol. Medication decisions depend on blood pressure stage, ASCVD risk, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease. Clinicians should consult the full guideline for treatment thresholds and follow-up. This is an educational summary for a university prototype.

title: ADA Standards of Care — Glycemic Targets overview (summary)
text: The American Diabetes Association Standards of Care emphasize individualized glycemic targets. For many nonpregnant adults, an A1C goal near less than 7% may be appropriate if it can be achieved safely without significant hypoglycemia. More or less stringent goals may be appropriate based on age, duration of diabetes, comorbidities, hypoglycemia risk, and patient preferences. Monitoring includes A1C and, when indicated, continuous glucose monitoring. Lifestyle therapy, metformin (when appropriate), and additional agents are selected based on cardiorenal risk, weight, cost, and efficacy. Always verify details in the current ADA Standards of Care. Educational prototype summary only.

title: Diabetes screening considerations for adults (summary)
text: Screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes is commonly considered in adults with overweight or obesity who have one or more risk factors, and in all adults beginning at recommended ages per current ADA guidance. Risk factors include family history, hypertension, dyslipidemia, physical inactivity, history of gestational diabetes, and certain high-risk race/ethnicity groups as described in guidelines. Diagnostic tests may include fasting plasma glucose, 2-hour OGTT, or A1C using validated assays. Abnormal results generally require confirmation. This summary is for RAG prototyping and must not replace clinical guidelines.

title: MedlinePlus — High Blood Pressure (patient/clinician-facing overview)
text: High blood pressure (hypertension) means the force of blood against artery walls is consistently too high. Many people have no symptoms. Untreated hypertension increases risk of heart attack, stroke, heart failure, and kidney disease. Measurement should use a validated technique. Treatment may include lifestyle changes and medicines prescribed by a clinician. MedlinePlus provides public government-curated health information. This excerpt is used as a public educational source in a research prototype.

title: MedlinePlus — Diabetes overview
text: Diabetes is a disease in which blood glucose levels are too high. Type 1 diabetes usually requires insulin. Type 2 diabetes is more common in adults and relates to insulin resistance; management may include lifestyle changes, oral medicines, and/or insulin. Complications can affect the eyes, kidneys, nerves, and heart. Public educational pages on MedlinePlus summarize symptoms, tests, and prevention themes. Clinicians should use professional guidelines for diagnosis and treatment decisions.

title: MedlinePlus — Cholesterol overview
text: Cholesterol is a fat-like substance in blood. High LDL cholesterol contributes to plaque buildup and coronary heart disease risk. HDL is often described as protective. Lifestyle approaches include healthy diet, exercise, and not smoking. Medicines such as statins may be recommended based on overall cardiovascular risk. MedlinePlus provides publicly available consumer health information curated with NIH resources.

title: AHRQ themes on shared decision making (summary)
text: The Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality highlights shared decision making as a collaborative process in which clinicians and patients make health decisions together, considering the best available evidence and patient values. Tools may include decision aids that present options, benefits, harms, and uncertainties. Shared decision making is especially relevant when guidelines recommend individualized choices, such as intermediate cardiovascular risk statin decisions. Educational prototype summary.

title: Educational abstract-style note: ASCVD risk estimation concepts
text: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk estimation tools use age, sex, race (in some equations), cholesterol, blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking status to estimate 10-year event risk. Risk estimates inform discussions about lifestyle and preventive therapies such as statins. Limitations include calibration across populations and uncertainty at intermediate risk. In clinical practice, risk estimates complement guidelines and patient preferences. This is a teaching summary for retrieval prototyping, not an original study abstract.

title: Educational note: Intensive BP control evidence themes
text: Randomized trials have evaluated intensive versus standard systolic blood pressure targets in selected high-risk adults. Intensive targets can reduce major cardiovascular events in some populations but may increase adverse events such as hypotension or electrolyte abnormalities. Applicability depends on age, frailty, comorbidities, and monitoring capacity. Guidelines translate trial evidence into staged hypertension definitions and treatment approaches. Prototype educational text only.

title: USPSTF Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes Screening (summary)
text: The USPSTF recommends screening for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 years who have overweight or obesity. Clinicians should offer or refer patients with prediabetes to effective preventive interventions. Screening intervals and follow-up should follow the full recommendation statement. This educational summary supports a university RAG prototype and is not a clinical order set.

title: MedQuAD-style sample Q/A — hypertension lifestyle
text: Question: What lifestyle changes help high blood pressure? Answer themes: reduce sodium, maintain healthy weight, exercise regularly, limit alcohol, manage stress, and take medicines as prescribed when indicated. This sample mimics MedQuAD-style consumer Q/A used for offline testing of retrieval pipelines. It is not live clinical advice.

title: Preventive cardiology lifestyle counseling themes
text: Lifestyle counseling for cardiovascular prevention commonly includes tobacco cessation, Mediterranean-style or DASH dietary patterns, at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity activity when appropriate, sleep health, and weight management. Lifestyle therapy is foundational before or alongside pharmacotherapy for blood pressure and lipids. Patient-specific barriers should be addressed. Educational prototype content with public heart.org lifestyle resource link.

title: PubMed Central open-access use note for prototypes
text: PubMed Central (PMC) archives full-text open-access biomedical literature. For university prototypes, teams may ingest openly licensed PMC articles subject to copyright and licensing terms. Retrieval systems should preserve article identifiers (PMCID/PMID) for citation. This document explains PMC as a source class for the pipeline rather than providing a single article body.

title: ACC/AHA cholesterol guideline themes — statin intensity in clinical ASCVD (summary)
text: In adults with clinical atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), high-intensity statin therapy is generally recommended to lower LDL cholesterol substantially when tolerated. High-intensity regimens typically reduce LDL-C by about 50% or more. If high-intensity therapy is not tolerated, use the maximum tolerated statin intensity. Additional nonstatin therapies may be considered for very high-risk patients who remain above LDL thresholds despite maximally tolerated statin therapy, per full guideline algorithms. Clinicians must consult the current ACC/AHA cholesterol guideline for exact drug options, monitoring, and exceptions. Educational prototype summary only.

title: USPSTF Hypertension Screening in Adults (summary)
text: The USPSTF recommends screening for hypertension in adults 18 years or older with office blood pressure measurement. The USPSTF recommends obtaining blood pressure measurements outside of the clinical setting for diagnostic confirmation before starting treatment. Screening intervals may be annual for adults 40 years or older and for adults at increased risk; adults 18 to 39 years with normal blood pressure and no risk factors may be screened less often (for example every 3 to 5 years) per the full recommendation. This educational summary supports a university RAG prototype and is not a clinical order set.

title: USPSTF Statin Primary Prevention (2016 archived / superseded summary)
text: ARCHIVED EDUCATIONAL SUMMARY: Older USPSTF statin primary-prevention statement. Superseded by later USPSTF recommendation. Retained to demonstrate ranking downgrades. Do not use for clinical decisions.

title: Evidence synthesis themes: statins for primary prevention (systematic review style)
text: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized trials generally support that statin therapy reduces major cardiovascular events in selected adults for primary prevention, with absolute benefit related to baseline risk. Educational Tier-2 synthesis-style summary for retrieval ranking demos.

title: Landmark RCT themes: intensive systolic BP targets in high-risk adults
text: Landmark multicenter randomized trials evaluated intensive versus standard systolic blood pressure targets in high-risk adults. Intensive targets reduced some cardiovascular events but increased certain adverse events. Educational Tier-3 prototype summary.
